lesson_title: The Men Who Owned the Gold
hook_text: In ten years, a mining camp became the biggest city in southern Africa. Who owned it?
clip_script: 1886. A gold reef is found on a farm on the Witwatersrand. But this is not river gold. It is fine specks in hard rock that slopes deep into the earth. To get it out you need shafts, crushers, chemicals and money, lots of money. Enter the Randlords: Rhodes, Beit, Wernher, Barnato, Robinson. Most made their first fortunes in Kimberley diamonds. They raise millions from investors in London and Europe. But there is a catch: the price of gold is fixed. So in 1887 they form the Chamber of Mines, a club for owners. They agree to keep black wages low, recruit workers from across southern Africa, and push the government for cheaper dynamite and stricter passes. Johannesburg booms. And the gold, and the power, flows to a few.
visual_style: A whiteboard ridge with a gold line sloping down underground, then portraits of the Randlords around a table labelled Chamber of Mines, with arrows from Mozambique, Lesotho and the Eastern Cape bringing workers.
pacing: Quick opening, steady middle, punchy ending.
